handlers.question: Which subdomains and hostnames have ever had a public SSL certificate under this domain, and since when?
handlers.why_it_matters: Certificate logs reveal forgotten sites, staging and test servers, old brands and how long the domain has been in real use, all without touching the company's systems.

handlers.question: Which email provider, sending services and SaaS tools does this domain's DNS show, and how is its email authentication set up?
handlers.why_it_matters: MX, SPF includes and verification TXT records show which mail provider and tools the company really uses, and how mature its email setup is.
handlers.source_name: Public DNS records (MX, SPF, TXT, NS)

handlers.question: Who issued the website's SSL certificate, when does it expire, and does it cover the domain?
handlers.why_it_matters: An expired, soon-to-expire or mismatched certificate is a basic sign of how well a site is looked after, and the issuer and dates are hard facts.

handlers.question: How long has this website existed in the Internet Archive, and in which years was it captured?
handlers.why_it_matters: The first capture shows how old the website really is, and gaps in the captures show years when it was down or not worth archiving. Each capture links to the archived page for anyone who wants to look.

handlers.question: Does the website link a YouTube channel, and when did that channel last post and how often?
handlers.why_it_matters: A channel the company advertises but stopped feeding long ago is a sign of abandoned marketing; an active one backs up claims of activity.
handlers.source_name: YouTube channel feed (linked from the company website)
